answer: Autonomous harvesters in an automated orchard prevent Sybil attacks by pulsing test signals along a conductive trellis line and measuring the return voltage ripple. Because digital emulation cannot fake real circuit dynamics, an adversary must deploy dedicated galvanic leads and interface hardware per identity, imposing steep capital costs. However, rainwater on foliage creates grounding shunts that distort measured impedances, occasionally disconnecting authentic harvesters.
